pages.title: Snapshots: snaprealms, SnapServer/SnapClient, metadata COW, snapshot ops, snapdiff and blockdiff

features.name: Snapshot creation (mkdir in .snap, CEPH_MDS_OP_MKSNAP 0x01400)
features.description: Creates a snapshot of a directory subtree: checks (allow_snaps flag, system dir, uid range, MAY_SNAPSHOT, subvolume, mds_max_snaps_per_dir, name rules), xlocks the dir snaplock, allocates a snapid from the rank-0 snap table (2PC), journals EUpdate('mksnap') with the table tid, applies, commits, notifies peers and clients, replies with the dir inode at the new snapid.
features.notes: Errors: EPERM (snaps disabled, system dir, uid, inside subvolume), EACCES (MDSAuthCaps lacks 's' or write), ENOTDIR, EMLINK, EEXIST, EINVAL (empty, >240, leading '_'), ENOSPC (full w/o MAY_FULL; also a preceding EACCES reply, double response), EROFS (read-only MDS), ESTALE (dir not in cache). No early reply. ETableServer PREPARE is journaled on rank 0 before the snapid is computed.

features.name: Snapshot removal (rmdir in .snap, CEPH_MDS_OP_RMSNAP 0x01401)
features.description: Removes an own snapshot of a directory: table DESTROY allocates a new seq, realm seq = last_destroyed = new seq, EUpdate('rmsnap'), notifications, reply, then purge of the dir's stale old_inodes; snapid and seq queued for removal in every data pool.
features.notes: '_'-prefixed (inherited) names: EINVAL; missing: ENOENT. Not gated by allow_new_snaps, system-dir, subvolume or max-snaps checks.

features.name: Snapshot rename (rename within .snap, CEPH_MDS_OP_RENAMESNAP 0x01403)
features.description: Renames an own snapshot; table UPDATE; realm seq unchanged (only last_modified/change_attr bump); EUpdate('renamesnap').
features.notes: No 240-byte length check on the new name; kernel never sees the change through traces.

features.name: Snapshot listing (CEPH_MDS_OP_LSSNAP 0x00402)
features.description: Lists snapshots visible in a directory's realm with id >= dir oldest_snap; own snapshots by plain name, inherited ones as _<name>_<ino decimal>; infinite LeaseStat with alternate_name; dir InodeStat at each snapid; pagination by last name (path2), max_entries/max_bytes; FRAG_END/FRAG_COMPLETE flags.
features.notes: Kernel NFS export also pages LSSNAP to map snapid -> name. cephfs-mirror ignores '_' names.

features.name: Snapshot lookup and traversal (.snap paths, CEPH_MDS_OP_LOOKUPSNAP 0x00400)
features.description: Wire path {ino=dir, path='/<snap>[/...]'}: empty first component = snapdir; snap name resolved by realm (plain or long name); traversal continues with dentry lookups at that snapid; LOOKUPSNAP handled as getattr returning the dir inode at the snapid.
features.notes: Kernel relies on ENOENT for a LOOKUP of the snapdir name to splice its local snapdir inode; libcephfs synthesizes the snapdir without asking the MDS. Snapshot paths take no path locks (rdlock_path_pin_ref).

features.name: Read-only snapshot access semantics
features.description: Mutations on snapshot paths return EROFS; open of a snapshot file for write is EROFS; open rdlocks the snapped inode filelock (waits for pending snapflush); snapped inodes get read-only caps without Capability objects (seq=mseq=realm=0); old_inodes only valid on the auth rank.
features.notes: POSIX requirement here means snapshots must not be writable and must present stable stat data.

features.name: Snapshot metadata (SnapPayload at mksnap, CEPH_MDS_OP_SNAP_METADATA 0x1406)
features.description: Key/value metadata per snapshot: set at creation from SnapPayload; modified by SNAP_METADATA with op_flag CREATE(1), CREATE|EXCL(3), REMOVE(4); returned in InodeStat.snap_metadata for inodes viewed at that snapid.
features.notes: cephfs-mirror stores primary_snap_id and checkpoint keys. MD op overwrites the snapshot stamp (ceph.snap.btime). No snaplock taken and no check_access (MDSAuthCaps not consulted; inferred). A request without data uses op_flag 3 = CREATE|EXCL and inserts an empty key. ENOENT after project_inode leaks the projection and the prepared table tid (inferred).

features.name: Snapshot attributes in InodeStat (snap_btime, snap_metadata, rstat.rsnaps, subvolume_id)
features.description: encode_inodestat includes SnapInfo.stamp (ceph.snap.btime) and metadata for the viewed snapid, rstat.rsnaps (ceph.dir.rsnaps: own snapshots counted per directory and summed) and the realm's subvolume ino.
features.notes: mgr/volumes reads ceph.snap.btime for snapshot info.

features.name: Snap realms and effective snapshot sets
features.description: SnapRealm per inode with srnode; effective set = own snaps + filtered past_parent_snaps + parent snaps since current_parent_since; global dummy realm (ino 3) holds all snaps; cached and lazily rebuilt; SnapContext derived from it.
features.notes: Realms are also created for quota dirs, subvolume roots, hard-linked inodes and inodes with past parents.

features.name: Snap trace encoding and delivery
features.description: Chain of ceph_mds_snap_realm records (old) or ENCODE_START(2,1) SnapRealmInfoNew (with last_modified, change_attr, flags) chosen by CEPHFS_FEATURE_NEW_SNAPREALM_INFO; sent in MClientReply.snapbl (NOSNAP requests only), MClientSnap, and cap IMPORT.
features.notes: Kernel never advertises NEW_SNAPREALM_INFO.

features.name: Realm notifications to clients (MClientSnap)
features.description: Per-realm notifications always sent with op SPLIT (split=realm ino, split_inos/split_realms only for a new realm) to every client with caps in the realm subtree; global notifications UPDATE/DESTROY with split=3 to every open/stale session on every rank for snap-table ops; reconnect UPDATE (split 0) for stale realm seqs; rollback merges as SPLIT to the parent.
features.notes: Sent on the session connection before the mksnap reply; counted messages (session seq).

features.name: Global snap table (SnapServer on rank 0) and SnapClient cache
features.description: Single monotonically increasing counter for snapids and destroy seqs; table ops CREATE/DESTROY/UPDATE via MDSTable 2PC with full-table NOTIFY_PREP to all ranks before AGREE; SnapClient caches committed + committing entries; sync at boot stages and before leaving reconnect.
features.notes: Table object mds_snaptable (version + SnapServer state + pending_for_mds); reset seeds last_snap from max data pool snap_seq. NOTIFY_PREP goes to every rank in state >= resolve, rank 0's own SnapClient included.

features.name: Metadata copy-on-write (first/last ranges, snapped dentries/inodes, old_inodes)
features.description: journal_cow_dentry preserves dentry/inode versions covered by snapshots: single-version inodes become separate snapped CInodes with snapped primary dentries; multiversion inodes (dirs, realms, nlink>1, existing old_inodes) get old_inodes entries; ancestor dirs pre-COWed in predirty_journal_parents; follows = global newest seq.
features.notes: Required for snapshots to show the namespace and attributes as of snapshot time.

features.name: Snapflush tracking for snapshots
features.description: On COW of a written file, clients with write caps must FLUSHSNAP the snapshot-time metadata; snapped inode locks forced into LOCK_SNAP_SYNC with wrlocks until flushed; null snapflush inferred when write caps are released; nudging after mds_freeze_tree_timeout/3; rebuilt at reconnect from snap_follows.
features.notes: Details on the capabilities page.

features.name: Lazy trimming of stale snapshot metadata
features.description: Deleted snapshots' dentries/inodes trimmed when dirfrags are fetched (snap_purged_thru) or committed (try_trim_snap_dentry); purge_stale_snap_data drops old_inodes; prune_past_parent_snaps for strays; stray dirs with past-parent snaps kept.

features.name: Propagation of removed snapshots to OSDs (MRemoveSnaps)
features.description: need_to_purge per data pool (snapid and destroy seq) sent to the monitor in MRemoveSnaps on every OSDMap change / tick; monitor marks them removed (new_removed_snaps, snap_seq, FLAG_SELFMANAGED_SNAPS) and echoes after commit; SnapServer journals SERVER_UPDATE to drop them.
features.notes: Requires mon cap 'osd pool rmsnap' (profile mds).

features.name: MDS-side SnapContext for MDS data operations
features.description: Stray purge, truncation and data uninlining use the inode realm's SnapContext so OSDs preserve clones for live snapshots.
features.notes: Also truncate_inode_write_finish (src/mds/MDCache.cc:6754); see page 3.2.

features.name: Hard-link global realm (PARENT_GLOBAL)
features.description: First hard link outside subvolumes gives the target a realm whose parent is the global realm, recording the primary parent's snapshots in past_parent_snaps (last_destroyed is reused as the primary parent's 'since' and reset to global seq + 1); unlinking a remote dentry records that dentry's dir-realm snaps since dn->first; all later filesystem snapshots cover it; cleared when back to one link.
features.notes: Hard links are POSIX; correct snapshot coverage of hard-linked files depends on this or an equivalent.

features.name: Past parent snapshots on rename/unlink
features.description: A primary inode that has a realm, or whose old realm's newest seq is >= its oldest_snap, gets a new srnode on unlink-to-stray or cross-realm rename: the old parent's snaps since current_parent_since go into past_parent_snaps and current_parent_since = global seq + 1.
features.notes: Details on the rename and namespace pages.

features.name: Subvolume realm restrictions (ceph.dir.subvolume)
features.description: SUBVOLUME flag on a realm: no nested subvolumes (EINVAL), mksnap only at the subvolume root (EPERM inside), cross-subvolume link/rename EXDEV, subvolume id reported to clients, optional subvolume-local COW seq.
features.notes: Natural shard boundary.

features.name: Snapshot visibility flag (ceph.dir.subvolume.snaps.visible)
features.description: SNAPDIR_VISIBILITY bit in an existing srnode, sent only in new-format traces; enforced by libcephfs when client_respect_subvolume_snapshot_visibility=true; not enforced by the MDS or kernel.
features.notes: mgr/volumes sets it on the subvolume root and, for sized subvolumes only, on the uuid data dir (whose quota realm would otherwise keep the default true). Bumps last_modified/change_attr, not seq.

features.name: Quota realm creation
features.description: Enabling a quota on a dir without srnode creates a realm so clients can locate quota roots by walking realms.
features.notes: Kernel get_quota_realm walks snap realms.

features.name: Snapshot policy limits
features.description: mds_max_snaps_per_dir (EMLINK, counts inherited snaps), name <= 240 bytes and not '_'-prefixed, uid range mds_snap_min_uid/max_uid, MAY_SNAPSHOT ('s' in MDS auth caps), allow_snaps MDSMap flag, system dirs refused, full cluster ENOSPC.

features.name: allow_multimds_snaps management and MULTIMDS_WITH_OLDSNAPS health
features.description: Rank 0 sets allow_multimds_snaps via mon command once no snapshot predates snaprealm_v2_since; mon refuses max_mds>1 otherwise and raises HEALTH_ERR.
features.notes: Legacy-format concern only.

features.name: Multi-MDS snapshot propagation
features.description: MMDSSnapUpdate (ino, op, srnode blob, tid) to all ranks >= resolve for table ops or to replicas for realm-only changes; snaplock state messages carry srnode; receivers notify_commit and notify their own clients; ISNAP xlock waits while replicas recover; snaplock rdlocks retained until safe.

features.name: Reconnect/rejoin snaprealm reconciliation
features.description: Client reconnect realms {ino, seq, parent}; stale seqs get UPDATE traces; caps in wrong realms get SPLIT; snapflush rebuilt; global UPDATE broadcast after open_snaprealms; reconnect waits for SnapClient sync.
features.notes: Possible SPLIT with split=0 when both conditions hit for one client (see page section 8).

features.name: Directory snapshot diff (CEPH_MDS_OP_READDIR_SNAPDIFF 0x01404)
features.description: Diffs one dirfrag between two snapshots: reports deleted entries at the older snapid and new/changed entries at the newer snapid, comparing attributes selected by CEPH_SNAPDIFF_* mask (default MTIME), waiting for pending snapflush; hash-ordered pagination; throttled like readdir.
features.notes: Used by cephfs-mirror SnapDiffSync.

features.name: File block diff between snapshots (CEPH_MDS_OP_FILE_BLOCKDIFF 0x01405)
features.description: MDS issues RADOS list_snaps on up to min(16, max_objects) data objects per call and returns changed extents between two snapshot versions as BlockDiff{rval (1=more, 0=done), scan_idx, interval_set blocks}; requires CEPHFS_FEATURE_BLOCKDIFF.
features.notes: Asserts in1->last <= in2->last on client input. No check_access (inferred). Extent math assumes stripe_count = 1; max_objects = 0 reports completion with no extents; hard-linked files resolve to one head CInode and report no diffs (all inferred from code).

features.name: Snapshot inode lookup by ino (LOOKUPINO with snapid) for NFS
features.description: Resolves (ino, snapid[, parent, hash]) to a snapped inode or head with snap data; ESTALE otherwise.
features.notes: Kernel knfsd snapshot file handles.

features.name: Admin: dump snaps [--server], perf counters, table tools
features.description: SnapClient cache dump or SnapServer dump on rank 0; per-op latency counters req_*snap*_latency, req_snapdiff_latency, req_blockdiff_latency, ceph_cap_op_flushsnap_ack, root_rsnaps; cephfs-table-tool snap reset/show.

features.name: mds_snap_rstat and mds_use_global_snaprealm_seq_for_subvol
features.description: mds_snap_rstat (false) maintains rstats of snapshot versions; mds_use_global_snaprealm_seq_for_subvol (true) controls which seq drives ancestor pre-COW.

serialization_points.name: mds_lock around all snapshot code
serialization_points.shared_state: realms, caches, snap table, client sessions
serialization_points.why_serialized: Single rank-wide lock; SnapRealm caches are mutable members rebuilt from const accessors.
serialization_points.notes: Blockdiff aggregation also re-enters under mds_lock via the finisher.

serialization_points.name: Rank-0 snap table 2PC with full-table NOTIFY_PREP fan-out
serialization_points.why_serialized: Globally unique monotonic snapid/seq allocation and every rank must know a pending snapshot before it is used.
serialization_points.notes: Each prepare journals ETableServer PREPARE (flushed) before computing the id, then waits for NOTIFY_ACK from every rank >= resolve (rank 0 included); entire table shipped each time.

serialization_points.name: xlock of target directory snaplock (mksnap/rmsnap/renamesnap)
serialization_points.shared_state: realm membership and srnode of the directory
serialization_points.why_serialized: Snapshot needs a stable cut of the subtree's realm; all requests below hold rdlocks on ancestor snaplocks.
serialization_points.notes: Blocks every in-flight and new path traversal under the dir, on all ranks (replica gather).

serialization_points.name: Ancestor snaplock rdlocks on every path-based request
serialization_points.why_serialized: Realm of a target must not change while a request runs.
serialization_points.notes: Conflicts with mksnap/rmsnap/rename/subvolume/quota realm changes on any ancestor.

serialization_points.name: Snaplock rdlocks retained until safe
serialization_points.why_serialized: Make later mksnap/setlayout (possibly on other ranks) wait for unsafe requests to journal.

serialization_points.name: ISNAP xlock waits for cluster recovery when degraded
serialization_points.why_serialized: Guarantee replayed requests and mksnap/setlayout are processed in proper order.

serialization_points.name: Global newest seq drives COW and new dentry first
serialization_points.why_serialized: One snapshot anywhere changes COW decisions everywhere (needed for hard links/renames across realms).
serialization_points.notes: mds_use_global_snaprealm_seq_for_subvol partially relaxes for ancestor pre-COW.

serialization_points.name: Global realm broadcast to every session
serialization_points.shared_state: all client sessions of each rank
serialization_points.why_serialized: Hard-linked inodes in PARENT_GLOBAL realms see every snapshot.
serialization_points.notes: Trace lists every snapshot in the filesystem.

serialization_points.name: Realm split on creation
serialization_points.why_serialized: Moves caps of descendant inodes to the new realm.
serialization_points.notes: Linear in inodes with caps of the parent realm, under mds_lock.

serialization_points.name: Realm BFS invalidate and notify
serialization_points.shared_state: realm subtree caches, per-client message map

serialization_points.name: All realm caches invalidated by any rmsnap
serialization_points.shared_state: cached snap sets/traces of every realm
serialization_points.notes: Lazy rebuild cost on next access.

serialization_points.name: Snapflush gating of snapped inodes
serialization_points.shared_state: snapped inode locks (LOCK_SNAP_SYNC), auth pins on head and snapped inode
serialization_points.why_serialized: Snapshot-time size/mtime only known after the client flushes its cap snap.
serialization_points.notes: Also blocks subtree freezing/migration via auth pins.

serialization_points.name: Per-rank MDLog ordering of snapshot EUpdates
Session-ordered notification before reply
serialization_points.why_serialized: Creator must have the new realm before seeing the reply.

serialization_points.name: Snap metadata op without snaplock
serialization_points.why_serialized: Relies on mds_lock and projection order only.
serialization_points.notes: Concurrent rmsnap can make it return ENOENT after projecting.

serialization_points.name: Snapdiff waits for snapflush via filelock rdlock
Removed-snap bookkeeping on rank 0
serialization_points.why_serialized: Single table; resent on each OSDMap until monitor echo.

external_contract.detail: Kernel does not advertise CEPHFS_FEATURE_NEW_SNAPREALM_INFO (19); it receives raw ceph_mds_snap_realm{ino, created, parent, parent_since, seq, num_snaps, num_prior_parent_snaps} + my_snaps + prior_parent_snaps (le64, descending) per realm, child first up to root/global realm.

Kernel replaces realm fields only when seq increases; parent is always re-checked; snap context = parent snaps >= parent_since + own + prior, seq = max(realm seq, parent seq). Any change the kernel must observe needs a seq bump.
A malformed trace makes the kernel set CEPH_MOUNT_FENCE_IO and blocklist itself.

Raw ceph_mds_snap_head{le32 op, le64 split, le32 num_split_inos, le32 num_split_realms, le32 trace_len} + inos + realms + trace. SPLIT moves split_inos into realm 'split' unless the inode's current realm.created > new realm.created; split_realms re-parented. Per-realm notifications are always op SPLIT; global ones UPDATE/DESTROY split=3.

Paths into snapshots are (dir ino, '/<snap>/...') with an empty first component; LOOKUP of the snapdir name must return ENOENT so the kernel splices its local snapdir inode; LOOKUPSNAP/LSSNAP/MKSNAP/RMSNAP/RENAMESNAP used for .snap operations; other mutations refused locally with EROFS.
Reply target InodeStat must be the directory ino with snapid = the snapshot id; kernel splices it to .snap/<name>. Replies for snapshots carry no snapbl.
LSSNAP returns own snapshots by name and inherited ones as _<name>_<ino decimal>; '_' names are rejected for MKSNAP/RMSNAP/RENAMESNAP with EINVAL.
Cap grants carry realm ino; the trace defining it must have been sent (reply snapbl or earlier), otherwise the kernel WARNs; readdir/lssnap do not issue caps across realm boundaries.
InodeStat carries snapid, snap_btime (ceph.snap.btime), rstat.rsnaps (ceph.dir.rsnaps), snap_metadata, subvolume_id.

For InodeStat at a snapid != NOSNAP the MDS issues read-only caps with seq = mseq = realm = 0 and no Capability object (cap_id and wanted are left uninitialized by the C++ MDS); the kernel only ORs the caps into i_snap_caps for snapped inodes.
LOOKUPINO with args.lookupino.snapid/parent/hash and LSSNAP paging to resolve snapshot file handles and names.
Quota roots are found by walking snap realms; every quota dir must be a realm.
On a new snapshot the kernel queues cap snaps (follows = old snapc seq), writes buffered data with the old snapc, and later sends FLUSHSNAP; MDS must ack FLUSHSNAP_ACK echoing follows and tid.

libcephfs advertises NEW_SNAPREALM_INFO and receives ENCODE_START(2,1){SnapRealmInfo, last_modified, change_attr, flags}; it updates a realm if seq or change_attr grew; keeps is_snapdir_visible. It decodes the new format iff the MDS advertised bit 19 in its session OPEN supported_features (the MDS decides from the client's bit), so both sides must agree.

external_contract.item: Snapdir synthesized locally with realm times
external_contract.detail: libcephfs never sends LOOKUP for the snapdir name: Client::_lookup returns a local (dir ino, CEPH_SNAPDIR) inode whose mtime/ctime are the realm's last_modified and change_attr the realm's change_attr (mode/uid/gid/atime/btime/size and system.* xattrs from the dir). The MDS must bump last_modified/change_attr on snapshot create/remove/rename/metadata/visibility changes for .snap stat to change.
Client::handle_snap asserts head.split != 0 for SPLIT and that the first trace element's ino equals head.split.
ceph_mksnap with SnapPayload metadata; ceph_do_snap_md_op data {key, value, u32 op_flag} with CREATE=1, EXCL=2, REMOVE=4; ceph_get_snap_info reads InodeStat.snapid and snap_metadata.
With client_respect_subvolume_snapshot_visibility=true, .snap lookups/mksnap/rmsnap return EPERM when the dir's realm lacks SNAPDIR_VISIBILITY (flag value 4).

Mirror uses LSSNAP (ignoring '_' names), snapshot metadata primary_snap_id and checkpoint keys, READDIR_SNAPDIFF (deleted at older snapid, existing at newer snapid in stx_dev) and FILE_BLOCKDIFF (loop while rval==1, scan_idx continuation, BlockDiff ENCODE_START(1,1){rval, scan_idx, interval_set}); blockdiff requires CEPHFS_FEATURE_BLOCKDIFF (23) or fails EOPNOTSUPP.

mgr/volumes mkdir/rmdir in <subvol>/.snap, reads ceph.snap.btime, sets ceph.dir.subvolume and ceph.dir.subvolume.snaps.visible; snap_schedule creates scheduled-<ts> snapshots and prunes with rmdir, keeping at most mds_max_snaps_per_dir - 1 (reads the MDS option via get_foreign_ceph_option).

MSG_REMOVE_SNAPS (90): Paxos header + map<int32 pool, vector<snapid>>; needs 'osd pool rmsnap' cap (granted by profile mds; without it the message is silently dropped); monitor records new_removed_snaps, raises snap_seq, sets FLAG_SELFMANAGED_SNAPS, echoes after commit (octopus+).

CEPH_MDSMAP_ALLOW_SNAPS (1<<1) gates mksnap (EPERM); CEPH_MDSMAP_ALLOW_MULTIMDS_SNAPS (1<<4) set by MDS via 'fs set allow_multimds_snaps true --yes-i-am-really-a-mds'; MULTIMDS_WITH_OLDSNAPS HEALTH_ERR.

All writers (clients, MDS purge/truncate/uninline) send SnapContext{seq, snaps desc}; snapids must stay above every data pool's snap_seq and never be reused; blockdiff reads list_snaps at CEPH_SNAPDIR on <ino>.<objno> objects.
mds_snaptable (ENCODE_START(5,3) SnapServer state) and srnode (sr_t ENCODE_START(8,4)) inside dentry InodeStore values are read by cephfs-table-tool and cephfs-data-scan; dump snaps output format.

rust_implications.implication: OSD SnapContexts require snapids that are unique per data pool, never reused and above pool snap_seq. A sharded design can lease monotonic id ranges to subvolume shards instead of a rank-0 2PC per snapshot, provided inodes never move between shards with different id ranges (subvolumes already forbid cross-subvolume rename/link with EXDEV).

The kernel only applies realm changes when seq grows and uses created to resolve split races; any snapshot create/destroy or parent change visible to clients must bump the realm seq monotonically, and new realms must get a created value >= older realms' created when they could race.

Must emit both trace formats: old raw ceph_mds_snap_realm for the kernel (no NEW_SNAPREALM_INFO) and SnapRealmInfoNew for libcephfs; chain must include every ancestor realm up to the root (or the global realm ino 3 for parent-global realms) and the union must equal the server-side snap set.

Before replying to MKSNAP/RMSNAP, the creating client's session must have the realm notification queued; other clients can be notified asynchronously. Per-realm notification can be shard-local (only clients with caps in the subvolume realm subtree).

The global realm (ino 3) only matters for clients holding caps on PARENT_GLOBAL (hard-linked, outside subvolume) inodes; if Rust confines hard links to subvolume realms or tracks which sessions hold such caps, it can avoid the every-session broadcast per snapshot op.

Always set head.split to the realm ino and the first trace element to that realm for SPLIT; libcephfs asserts on it. Kernel tolerates SPLIT with empty lists; per-realm updates may use SPLIT like the C++ MDS or UPDATE.

On-disk format is free, but the externally visible results must match: dentries/inodes as of each snapshot for lookup/readdir/getattr in .snap paths, read-only caps, EROFS for writes, ceph.snap.btime, snap metadata, rsnaps. Per-subvolume seqs (like mds_use_global_snaprealm_seq_for_subvol=false) avoid global COW coupling when subvolumes confine renames/links.

Must implement FLUSHSNAP handling (follows -> next snap), null snapflush inference, and gating of snapshot-version reads until flushed, otherwise snapshot file sizes/mtimes are wrong; this is per-inode and need not block subtree operations.

C++ blocks all requests under the directory (snaplock xlock vs ancestor rdlocks retained until safe). A Rust engine can take a shard-level epoch/barrier instead: new requests see the new snap seq, in-flight unsafe mutations must be ordered (journal position) relative to the snapshot; only realm membership changes truly conflict.

Rust must send MRemoveSnaps (pool -> snapids) for each data pool with an entity holding 'osd pool rmsnap', persist pending removals until the monitor echo, and keep using realm SnapContexts for its own purge/truncate/uninline writes.

To keep cephfs-mirror incremental sync working, implement READDIR_SNAPDIFF (exact entry/snapid semantics, mask, hash order pagination) and FILE_BLOCKDIFF (advertise CEPHFS_FEATURE_BLOCKDIFF bit 23, BlockDiff encoding, rval 1/0 continuation, list_snaps based extents) and validate inputs (C++ asserts on snapshot order).

Preserve name rules (no '_' prefix, 240 bytes), long-name format for inherited snapshots, EMLINK limit semantics (decide whether to count inherited snaps), uid range options, MAY_SNAPSHOT auth cap, allow_snaps MDSMap flag, subvolume EPERM rule, and the vxattrs ceph.dir.subvolume, ceph.dir.subvolume.snaps.visible.
Deleted snapshot metadata can be reclaimed lazily per shard; there is no client-visible deadline except that LSSNAP/lookups must stop showing the snapshot immediately.
A fresh Rust filesystem has no legacy snapshots; it should still set or tolerate CEPH_MDSMAP_ALLOW_MULTIMDS_SNAPS so the monitor allows max_mds > 1 and no MULTIMDS_WITH_OLDSNAPS health error appears.

rust_implications.topic: Access checks on snapshot side channels
rust_implications.implication: C++ performs no MDSAuthCaps check for SNAP_METADATA and FILE_BLOCKDIFF (inferred). A Rust MDS can apply MAY_WRITE|MAY_SNAPSHOT to metadata ops and MAY_READ to blockdiff to close a path-restriction bypass, after checking that the caps cephfs-mirror and mgr are deployed with include those flags (not verified here); validate op_flag explicitly instead of defaulting to 3.

C++ never rolls back a prepared snap-table tid when the request fails after AGREE. A Rust allocator should release or abort reserved ids/seqs on request failure or kill (ids may still be burned, but pending state must not accumulate) and must never leave a projected srnode behind on an error path.

Old vs new trace format is chosen by the client's feature bit on the MDS side but by the MDS's advertised bit on the libcephfs side; a Rust MDS must advertise CEPHFS_FEATURE_NEW_SNAPREALM_INFO exactly when it is prepared to send SnapRealmInfoNew to clients that advertise it, and keep last_modified/change_attr meaningful because libcephfs exposes them as the .snap directory's mtime/ctime/change_attr.

Check own snapshots under the locks used for the final emptiness check (C++ checks them only in an unlocked pre-check that is skipped with a cached filelock), or keep stray directories with own snapshots alive, so a directory's snapshots cannot be orphaned.

FILE_BLOCKDIFF compares clone snaps against in->last, which can be a seq value that is not a snapshot id; can this miss changes?
FILE_BLOCKDIFF asserts in1->last <= in2->last on client-controlled ordering; libcephfs does not order the arguments.
Is the snapshot stamp rewrite in handle_client_snap_md_op (ceph.snap.btime changes on metadata update) intended?
mds_max_snaps_per_dir counts inherited (parent and past-parent) snapshots and is skipped for directories without a realm; intended semantics?
renamesnap does not enforce snapshot_name_max (240) on the new name; intended?
Does any kernel path depend on receiving the global realm (ino 3) update when the client holds no caps in PARENT_GLOBAL realms?
Is removing the destroy seq ids (in addition to snapids) from the OSD pools required for correctness, or only defensive?
When the cluster is full and the client lacks the f cap, dispatch_client_request lets check_access reply EACCES and then replies ENOSPC again on the same MDRequest; is the double response harmless?
handle_client_snap_md_op and handle_client_file_blockdiff never call check_access; is the lack of any MDSAuthCaps check (path restriction, 's' flag) intended? Inferred from code.
SNAP_METADATA with no data defaults op_flag to 3, which is CREATE|EXCL (valid) despite the comment calling it invalid; an empty request inserts an empty metadata key. Intended?

SNAP_METADATA returning ENOENT after project_inode (Server.cc:12146-12149) leaves the projected inode/srnode on the directory and the prepared table tid uncommitted; what happens to the next mutation of that directory? Inferred, not reproduced.

rmdir/rename-over-dir checks own snapshots only in _dir_is_nonempty_unlocked, which returns early when the filelock is cached; can a directory with own snapshots be removed and then purged (its snapshots orphaned in the table and on OSDs)? Inferred, not reproduced.
FILE_BLOCKDIFF computes extents as contiguous per object (Striper::get_file_offset(objno, 0) + size); is it wrong for layouts with stripe_count > 1?
